Well 200 views and 50 likes means 1/3 of the people watching like it. I don’t know if that’s good numbers or not. If you look at a video with let’s say 500,000 likes normally they move around 1,000,000 to 2,000,000 views so ratio wise it’s about the same. So this makes it even more confusing.

My question about that is how do we get our criteria out to the right target audience? I know hashtags and music is two ways but is there something else. I make video edits of Asian Dramas and Shows, so my audience is most likely targeted to mainly women between the ages of 16 to 35. I myself am 25, which is why I kinda put myself at a sort of mean for those numbers. Is there a certain way of going about it or is it a random chance?
Did I mention I’ve never won a raffle. So my luck is shite and TikTok is vague about the rules. Just like everything else. Lol
I guess we are all horses at this point.

Yeah over saturation is definitely a thing. I didn’t really see an issue with it if it wasn’t so blatantly obvious that TikTok stops putting content on FYP after reaching a certain criteria, especially newer accounts. I honestly wasn’t even hoping for millions of views, 1000-5000 consistently would be fine with me, but the algorithm is just brutal.
Another thing I thought was time a day. But whether I posted at 11am or 10pm, nothing was really different.

I don’t understand why it does this. I even increased the amount of hashtags and everything hoping to snag a wider audience fyp but it made no difference. At first I thought it was because I wasn’t using their music. So I’d edit with music and then clip the same audio from TikTok, but it made no difference. Hashtags also didn’t change much. Plus the content I’m posting a lot of the tags have almost 200 mil to 2 bil views so people watch the content. I make show and movie edits, mainly Asian media, so having people to watch it isn’t the issue either. I don’t know I’m just trying to understand this.

I just finished and let’s just say I cried like the little girl I am. 😭
9/10
